messages:
mike_r: quick heads-up — ran a KV cache profile on mixtral-8x with GQA vs MQA layouts, saw weird fragmentation when we hit >1.6M kv entries :thinking_face:
anya_k: can you paste the profiling output? was this on the paged layout or slab?
mike_r: paged. short dump:
```
> trace: kv_pages_allocated=18432
> kv_frag_runs=37
> avg_page_fill=0.46
> num_kv_heads=64 (GQA config) vs 12 (MQA effective)
> tail_latency_99=78ms -> 210ms after fragmentation
```
kevin_s: 210ms tail is alarming. did kernel selection change for that run (int8 path)?
mike_r: nope, same kernel set as baseline. only changes were: bump num_key_value_heads to 64 to match Llama head layout + enabling continuous batching heuristic (batch window 6ms)-> which increased concurrent KV touch frequency.
liz: interesting — more heads increases per-token KV lookup overhead and worsens page locality. with paged layout, head stride causes scattering across pages.
anya_k: does MQA help here? fewer physical kv heads should increase locality but also change kernel vectorization assumptions.
mike_r: we tried MQA mapping (pack heads) — throughput improved by ~12% but some queries saw generation glitches (repeated tokens) during beam regen. probably kernel/kv alignment bug.
sre-carol: any regressions flagged by canary? did this affect production?
kevin_s: canary showed slight uptick in retries on dedicated pools at 03:40, correlated with the experiment window. infra-bot: incident-created #1974130012 — autoscale fallback triggered twice.
liz: profiling suggests two main culprits: (1) increased page churn due to head interleaving, (2) batch coalescing pushing more long-context requests into the same KV working set.
anya_k: for RoPE scaling — did we convert positional dims or scale factor? RoPE scaling mismatch can change per-head compute and slow down kernels.
mike_r: RoPE scaling was enabled (scale=1.25 for mixtral-8x long-context test). That increased per-step matmul cost ~6% in hot path.
kevin_s: recommendation: revert continuous batch-window from 6ms -> 3ms for now, enable MQA packing only with kernel alignment patch, and add a soft cap on per-request kv-pages touched (like 512).
liz: +1. also adding a cache-tiling pass to remap K/V pages by head groups could recover locality without forcing MQA globally.
anya_k: I'll add a perf test matrix: (num_kv_heads={12,32,64}, rope_scale={1.0,1.25}, batch_window_ms={3,6}, layout={paged,slab,MQA-packed}). aim to run on dedicated-qa tonight.
mike_r: thanks. one more ask — can runtime emit a compact per-request KV-extract sample in traces (page_ids touched, head_bitmap) so we can diagnose fragmentation without full dumps?
kevin_s: doable. I'll prototype an opt-in trace field and have infra-bot post a sample to this thread when ready.
anya_k: filing follow-ups: gh-rt-1422 (tiling remap PR), gh-rt-1423 (KV trace proto), gh-rt-1424 (batch-window tuning job).
sre-carol: schedule a canary for gh-rt-1422 after QA. if patch prevents autoscale fallback, we can roll to prod. :thumbsup:
mike_r: copy. will post perf artifacts and flamegraphs here once jobs finish.
infra-bot: perf-job/1974129999 completed: mixtral-8x paged vs slab comparison uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/mixtral/1974129999/report.html
kevin_s: I'll grab the report and run kernel-selection analyzer tomorrow AM.
mike_r: thanks all — keeping this thread as the source of truth for the tuning run.
